claims.text: Noble metal–based high-entropy alloys are synthesized from diverse element mixtures.
Existing noble metal–based HEAs have uncontrolled, complex surface structures.
An integrated framework combining DFT, molecular dynamics, and improved interatomic potentials can predict noble metal–based HEA behavior.
The simulation framework can guide self-assembly into three-dimensional nanoframeworks with atomic-level precision.
Atomic-level control of three-dimensional nanoframework formation will enhance catalytic performance.
Improved atomistic simulations can accurately model nucleation, growth, and atomic diffusion during synthesis.
Simulation predictions can be used to steer HEA self-assembly during synthesis.
The proposed framework is applicable under ambient to moderately elevated, catalytically relevant temperatures.
Atomic-scale nucleation and growth govern the formation of interconnected HEA nanostructures.
Atomic diffusion can drive phase separation in noble metal–containing HEA nanoparticles.
Atomistic simulation can capture structural and chemical evolution associated with atomic diffusion.
Predictive simulation guidance will produce well-ordered three-dimensional nanoframeworks with enhanced active sites.
Conventional synthesis methods yield irregular and uncontrolled HEA morphologies.
Simulation-guided HEA catalysts will have greater surface area than conventionally synthesized HEAs.
Simulation-guided HEA catalysts will have more uniformly distributed active sites than conventionally synthesized HEAs.
Simulation-guided HEA catalysts will exhibit improved catalytic efficiency relative to conventionally synthesized HEAs.
Unmodeled kinetic barriers or environmental factors could reduce the predictive accuracy of the simulation framework.
